reason: The text explicitly depicts Yahweh displaying antagonistic behavior toward the Hebrew people. Yahweh tells Moses: 'Let me alone, that my wrath may burn hot against them, and that I may consume them' (וְיִֽחַר־ אַפִּי בָהֶם וַאֲכַלֵּם), and describes them as 'stiff-necked people' (עַם־ קְשֵׁה־עֹרֶף). Yahweh explicitly threatens to destroy them and establish Moses as a new nation instead. However, this antagonism is specifically provoked by the people's transgression (construction and worship of the golden calf), and critically, Yahweh relents from His threatened judgment when Moses intercedes on their behalf ('And the Lord repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people'). The antagonism shown is therefore neither unprovoked nor permanent, but rather a response to covenant violation that can be mitigated through proper intercession.
